verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown in the Pacific on Friday ... off the San Diego coast'; R2: 'splashed into the Pacific Ocean just after 8 p.m. Eastern on Friday'; R3: 'splash down at about 8:07 p.m. ET Friday, April 10, 2026, off the coast of San Diego, California'; R4: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on April 10'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm location, date, time, and ocean with exact or near-exact details.

verifications.claim: The splashdown was a parachute-assisted landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'six-minute blackout that preceded the opening of the parachutes'; R3: 'parachute-assisted water landing'; R5: 'Parachute Deployment ... three main parachutes, which then slow the spacecraft down to roughly 30 km/h'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe parachutes deploying for the splashdown landing.

verifications.claim: The splashdown concluded a 10-day mission around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'nearly 10-day flight'; R3: '10-day journey around the moon'; R4: '10-day moon voyage ... 9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes and 15 seconds -- though NASA rounds up and calls it a 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state or round to a 10-day mission duration around the moon.

verifications.claim: The crew returned home for recovery by U.S. Navy and NASA teams.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery ship USS John P. Murtha ... NASA and the Defense Department teamed up'; R3: 'U.S. Navy recovery vessel ... NASA's Johnson Space Center'; R4: 'US Navy USS John P. Murtha ... NASA and US military personnel'; R5: 'recovery teams, consisting of the U.S. Navy, Airforce and NASA'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm U.S. Navy and NASA involvement in recovery post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule re-entered Earth's atmosphere at roughly 25,000 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'hit the atmosphere travelling Mach 33 ... 24,661 mp/h (39,668 km/h)'; R3: 'slow the capsule from about 25,000 mph'; R5: 'entering the Earth’s atmosphere at approximately 40,000 km/h'; R6: 'fiery plunge through the atmosphere at nearly 25,000mph'
verifications.reasoning: Sources give speeds equivalent to or directly stating roughly 25,000 mph at re-entry.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule utilized drogue chutes and then three main parachutes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'two smaller drogue parachutes ... three main parachutes'; R5: 'two drogue shoots ... three main parachutes'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe drogue chutes followed by three main parachutes.

verifications.claim: The parachutes slowed the capsule to about 30 km/h for the final splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'slowing to a 19 mp/h (30 km/h) splashdown'; R3: 'slow Orion from about 130 mph to just 17 mph'; R5: 'slow the spacecraft down to roughly 30 km/h'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm parachutes reduce speed to approximately 30 km/h (or equivalent mph) for splashdown.

verifications.claim: Inflatable bags were deployed following the splashdown to ensure the capsule remained upright.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'five orange airbags will inflate ... flip the capsule into an upright position'; R5: 'flotation devices systems will be deployed to keep the capsule upright'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe inflatable airbags or flotation devices for upright stability post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: Recovery crews were on standby following the splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The recovery ship USS John P. Murtha awaited the crew’s arrival'; R4: 'Navy personnel were waiting for the crew ... positioned off the San Diego coast'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state recovery ships and personnel were waiting/positioned for immediate post-splashdown action.

verifications.claim: Recovery crews aimed to get the crew out of the capsule within approximately two hours.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the crew would exit the vehicle ... within about two hours'; R4: 'expected to take about an hour ... nearly two hours ago'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify recovery timeline of about two hours or less to extract crew.
